text:
maria (support): Hey team, customer (AcmeRetail) reporting 429s during a product demo. They say they upgraded to Pro last week but are still getting throttled. Error snippets attached. Can someone confirm if this looks like plan cap vs burst exhaustion?

sam (infra): Can you paste the response headers and the API key prefix? Quick check: `x-rw-quota`, `x-rw-remaining`, `x-rw-burst-remaining` usually tell the story.

maria (support): From their logs: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`
`Retry-After: 30`
`x-rw-plan: pro-monthly`
`x-rw-remaining: 0`
`x-rw-burst-remaining: 0`
`x-rw-until-reset: 2027-11-02T13:10:12Z`

sam (infra): OK that shows they exhausted both steady-state quota and burst. Could be either their transformation is sending many parallel requests or they have a per-minute bucket drained. Do we have their usage pattern?

maria (support): They said they were doing parallel generation for slide previews (~20 concurrent requests) during demo. They thought Pro included enough headroom for that. Their account ID: acct_0a9c. Attached billing note: upgrade completed on 2027-10-30.

jules (sales): FYI, Pro has a concurrency and sustained token/sec cap — we document it in the plan page but customers often expect unlimited burst. We can offer a short-term burst increase or move them to Dedicated. maria, can you confirm expected peak TPS and whether they want a temporary lift for the demo only?

maria (support): Customer asks for a same-day temporary lift for the demo (3 hours). They also asked if there's a way to queue/retry client-side instead of requesting an exception.

sam (infra): For immediate mitigation, two options: 1) Give a small temporary burst allowance tied to their API key (safest operationally), or 2) suggest client backoff/retry with jitter and limited concurrency. Example guidance we give: `max_concurrency=4` and exponential backoff starting at 200ms.

maria (support): Can you draft the exact retry snippet I can send them? Also who owns temporary bursts? sales or infra?

sam (infra): Paste this to customer: ```
# pseudo-code
semaphore = Semaphore(4)
for job in jobs:
  with semaphore:
    attempt=0
    while attempt < 5:
      resp = call_redwood_api(job)
      if resp.status != 429:
        break
      sleep(2 ** attempt * 0.2 + random() * 0.1)
```
Explain: limit concurrency to 4 and backoff, this drastically reduces token-rate spikes.

natalie (billing): For temporary bursts we need a sales-approved note (audit trail). Jules, can you confirm approval? We'll need to annotate invoice if we offer a complimentary lift beyond plan.

jules (sales): I can approve a one-time 3-hour burst for AcmeRetail as a courtesy to preserve the deal. Please tag it as "sales_burst_trial" and set a limit: extra 200k tokens for that window. I'll follow-up with a short email.

maria (support): Thanks. What is the operational process to apply the burst to acct_0a9c?

sam (infra): Ops-bot can apply an override if you provide account ID, window start/end, and token allowance. I'll queue the change once I see the exact window. We should also add a guard: auto-revert at end time.

ops-bot: Scheduled quota override request received for acct_0a9c. Please confirm parameters: start=2027-11-02T14:00:00Z, end=2027-11-02T17:00:00Z, extra_tokens=200000. Reply with `confirm` to apply.

maria (support): confirm

ops-bot: Override applied. acct_0a9c now has a temporary +200000 token allowance from 2027-11-02T14:00:00Z to 2027-11-02T17:00:00Z. Auto-revert enabled.

maria (support): I sent the retry snippet and told them we've applied the 3hr burst. They also asked what the long-term solution is — prefer not to go Dedicated right now. Any guidance?

sam (infra): Long-term: 1) Recommend batching slides into fewer calls (reduce prompt tokens per request), 2) Use prefix caching if slides share common template, 3) Evaluate per-minute quota bump or move to Reserved capacity. Also consider model quantization / lower max_tokens to cut unit consumption. I can run a quick perf estimate if they share sample prompts and concurrency targets.

jules (sales): I'll open an upsell sheet and propose: 1) Increase to Pro+ (higher sustained throughput) or 2) 3-month trial of Dedicated at reduced rate if they're willing to commit. I'll own follow-up with procurement.

maria (support): Great. I'll close the support ticket with the mitigation applied and note Jules will follow for commercial options. Any follow-ups for infra?

sam (infra): Please collect a 10–20-request sample trace when they run the demo and drop it here if they still see 429s after the burst. If 429s continue, we need to check whether the API key is mis-tagged to an older plan or if there is a bug preventing override from counting.

maria (support): Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
